stem.text: Proteins which transport sugars out of cells have been identified. These proteins are called SWEETs. Each SWEET has seven coiled, cylindrical regions which together make up a pore through the cell surface membrane bilayer, as shown in the diagram.

stem.alt: Diagram of seven coiled cylindrical regions forming a pore through a cell surface membrane bilayer, regions numbered 1 to 7

stem.text: What describes each of the seven coiled regions (1-7) of a SWEET shown in the diagram?

A.text: primary structure held in its shape by bonds such as hydrogen bonds

B.text: primary structure held in its shape by peptide bonds

C.text: secondary structure held in its shape by bonds such as hydrogen bonds

D.text: secondary structure held in its shape by peptide bonds
